notes: Correctly classifies response-reading expressions with good unit and integration tests, but it puts reverse_proxy-specific placeholder knowledge (and speculative rp./static-concat handling) into the generic caddyhttp MatchExpression and hand-rolls a recursive AST walker instead of using the ast visitor, and the doc update drops the is_transport_error mention.

Correctly classifies retry expressions from the checked CEL AST, covering dynamic names, escaped literals, look-alike names and even folded literal concatenation, but the hand-rolled recursive walker is verbose and it puts reverse-proxy-specific placeholder knowledge (including an `rp.` shorthand heuristic) into the generic caddyhttp matcher.

Closely mirrors the reference by collecting static placeholder names plus a dynamic flag from the checked CEL AST with ast.PostOrderVisit, then classifying them in reverseproxy using exact response names and the header prefix; its classification table and POST integration test are solid, but it accidentally deleted the doc comment on brokenUpstreamAddr.

Closely mirrors the reference design (MatchExpression exposes static placeholder names plus a dynamic flag, and reverseproxy decides which names are response data) with good classification and behavioral tests, but it accidentally deletes the doc comment on brokenUpstreamAddr.

The classification logic is sound, but it re-parses each expression with a separate parser, precomputes the result as Handler state that only Provision sets (so handlers built directly, as in the existing and hidden tests, lose all response-based retries), moves placeholder expansion into a new internal package unnecessarily, and churns every test helper call site.

The classification logic is right in production, but caching `responseRetryMatchers` at Provision makes an unprovisioned handler silently stop response-based retries (hidden tests fail), and it re-parses each expression with a separate parser, moves the placeholder regexes into a new internal package, and changes the test helper signature.
